James Talarico

Democratic candidate for U.S. Senator, Texas · Open seat

State representative; former middle school teacher

James Talarico is a Democratic state representative from Austin, now in his fourth term in the Texas House, and a former middle school teacher in San Antonio ISD. He won the March 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate over U.S. Rep. Jasmine Crockett. In the November 3, 2026 general election he faces Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton and Libertarian Ted Brown.

Where Talarico stands

Gas tax
Proposes suspending federal taxes on gasoline and diesel to lower fuel costs.
Data centers
Says data centers should pay for their own electricity infrastructure, lose their tax exemptions, and have less impact on local communities. Criticizes tax breaks given to data center companies.
Iran and war powers
Says he would support passing a war powers resolution to stop the war with Iran, arguing it has left both countries worse off.
Border wall in Big Bend
Opposes the border wall in Big Bend, which he calls a 'monument to corruption.' Released a border security plan and has criticized both Biden-era border policies and the wall.
Gender care for minors
Asked about a federal ban on gender transition care for minors, said: 'I do not support gender reassignment surgery for minors.'
Marijuana and hemp
Supports legal, regulated adult-use marijuana, with tax revenue going to public safety and health programs.
Tariffs
Says he would vote 'to repeal these crazy tariffs,' arguing they raise costs for families.
Congressional ethics
Proposes banning members of Congress from trading individual stocks and setting term limits of six House terms and two Senate terms.
Transgender athletes
Said on Fox News: 'I oppose trans athletes playing in girls' sports if it endangers safety or fairness.'
